reason: Both catch the same core defects (mutable default, index-out-of-range, division by zero, in-place sort, and the same-call dedup/under-fill logic bug), but Response A correctly notes that top_scores([]) with the default limit=5 hits the IndexError before ever reaching the division, and pins the ZeroDivisionError to the limit=0 case, whereas Response B asserts 'top_scores([]) raises ZeroDivisionError' without that caveat, which is actually false under the default arguments. A's dedup example is also more concrete and demonstrates the under-fill precisely.
